title: Prove a fifth rational frame needs eight calls for every rational slope, settling the #2112 seven-call case (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Scoped proof in a formal register model (no new κ).** For the four-role target `diag([A+P],[A+Q],[B+P],[B+Q])` of [PR #2085](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2085), extended by the fifth rational rank-one address `R_t = (1,t)^T(1,t)`, the exact minimum number of paid calls is **eight for every rational `t`**.

At `t = 1/2` this settles the seven-call case left open by [PR #2112](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2112): its `7 ≤ min ≤ 8` becomes `min = 8`. It also answers #2085's open question for the whole slope family.

Proof outline (full proof in the package README):

1. **Exponent support.** Expanding `∏ (I+N_j) + [F_j]N_j` shows every monomial has exponent equal to a subset sum of the labels, as rational matrices. So each target frame is a nonnegative sum of labels with multiplicities bounded by the label counts. With at most seven calls, `R_t` can enter such a sum only at `t = 0` (exact enumeration over all rational `t`). For `t ≠ 0`, each of `A, B, P, Q` is therefore used.
2. **Odd denominator.** `Λ_t/Λ` has odd order, so `L/2L` is the old lattice mod 2 and `R_t ≡ A` or `0`. The #2085 rank/trace floor of 8 applies at every word length.
3. **Even denominator.** `B ∈ 2Λ_t`, and `A, P, R_t` give a basis mod 2. A word using `R_t` needs an even number (at least 2) of `R_t` calls, at least one `B` call by step 1, and at least 5 `A/P/Q` calls. The last bound is an exact minimum over all 65,536 masks. Total: 8. A word without `R_t` has the #2085 floor of 8.

The direct eight-call word attains 8.

## Evidence and reproduction

Package: `research/bit-fifth-rational-frame-every-rational-t`. From the repository root, using CPython 3.12 (`~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12` locally):

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/bit-fifth-rational-frame-every-rational-t/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-fifth-rational-frame-every-rational-t
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/bit-fifth-rational-frame-every-rational-t --check-source-history
```

All three pass locally. The verifier takes about 0.5 s and prints:

```text
PASS_FIFTH_RATIONAL_FRAME_EVERY_T_EXACT_MINIMUM_8 grid_odd=949 grid_even=482 support_exceptions=['0'] idempotents=120 odd_floor=8 even_visible_floor=5 even_total=8 mutated_visible_floor=3 direct_calls=8
```

It recomputes:

- every finite input: support exceptions, both first-order minima and the 120 idempotents;
- the parity classification of `Λ_t/2Λ_t` on 1,431 reduced slopes;
- the direct word, by exact multiplication in the group algebra.

Two controls must fail: dropping one call, and a mutated mask.

## Limitations

- The general lattice classification (step 2/3) is a hand proof in the README. The grid check supports it but does not prove it. No proof-assistant verification.
- Only the one-parameter family `R_t` is covered. Scaled addresses `c·R_t`, other rank-one frames, two added frames and other targets are not covered.
- Formal paid-call model only: frame construction, additions, precision and interface charges are excluded. No supplier mapping or κ change.
- #2112's six-call enumeration is cited, not rechecked. This proof does not depend on it.

## Open next questions

- Can a scaled rational rank-one address `c v^T v`, or a pair of added frames, lower eight? First step: classify the addresses that can enter a target's exponent support within seven calls.
- Can exponent support plus the first-order floor decide other open minimum-length cases in torsion-free address models without word enumeration? The blocker is targets with several supports.

## Related open work

No open PR studies this target or the `R_t` alphabet (rechecked after CI, including this account's #6037–#6039, which study other objects). The predecessors #2085 and #2112 are merged.
